adjudication.evidence: P1 (462–465) and P2 (463–478) overlap and both show a large positive offset (~11,10,12 MAD) in N/E/U; however, the original observations show a single sustained jump at ~462–463 followed by gradual decay—not a return to pre-jump level—so no opposing return exists. P3 (476–477) is a brief negative spike (~−11,−9,−12 MAD) but occurs *within* the decaying tail of the earlier jump and lacks a preceding sustained platform; it appears as an isolated spike, not a temporary platform. P4 (517–519) shows small offsets (~−1.7, +1.7, 0 MAD); residual plots and hypothesis tests show no persistent platform—only noise-level fluctuation. P5 (529) is a single-day dip with no sustained interval; residuals remain noisy and no return is observed. No candidate satisfies the definition: sustained shift + opposing return across same axes. Hence, replace with empty set.
